subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw accept `gateway.peers` as a narrow core cross-gateway session-routing contract now, or require the broader federation identity/scope design before adding this security-sensitive surface?
rationale: The patch is a feature with new config, credentials, message-delivery, and session-state behavior across Gateway trust boundaries; the code defects are concrete, but the permanent API and security model require maintainer intent.

options.title: Define federation contract first
options.body: Keep this PR paused and use the canonical issue plus federation FRD to settle peer identity, URL policy, scopes, delivery guarantees, and session-history semantics before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow peer feature
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the `gateway.peers` direction, then require this PR to remove raw URL bypasses, repair remote spawn, rebase cleanly, and provide live proof.

options.title: Defer to external bridge/plugin paths
options.body: If core federation is out of scope for now, document supported external bridge/plugin patterns and close or supersede this implementation after preserving the useful context.

recommendation.title: Define federation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this PR paused and use the canonical issue plus federation FRD to settle peer identity, URL policy, scopes, delivery guarantees, and session-history semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-tool and linked-issue routing history makes this the best available owner for deciding the session-tool contract, with security input still needed.
